_note: Documentation only: no code reads this file at runtime. It records the public figures behind Nas, with the status of each, for the team and for the assumptions table. Status: ANCHORED = the team opened the source URL and checked the figure (MoDEE figures on 2026-10-09; 'retrieved' where recorded); TEAM_CONFIRMED = confirmed by the team, no source link recorded yet; CITED_UNVERIFIED = quoted by our AI-assisted desk research (Qwen, 'Amman in a Box') with a source we could not open or confirm (VALIDATION.md and seed_census.py call these CITED). The 26 engine constants in sim/assumptions.py are all ASSUMPTION; entries here only give context for them. Never present a CITED_UNVERIFIED figure as an official statistic. Last checked 2026-10-10.

internet_use_individuals_jordan.source_name: MoDEE 2024 Household ICT Usage and Access Survey (results announcement)
internet_use_individuals_jordan.quote: The proportion of individuals who used the internet increased from 92.5% in 2023 to 95.6% in 2024.
internet_use_individuals_jordan.notes: National, all ages; no age breakdown on the page. seed_census.py uses it as the share of synthetic adults with a smartphone and hits it exactly (95.6%, 956 of 1,000). The age gradient (older people more often without one) is an ASSUMPTION.

smartphone_households_amman.source_name: MoDEE 2024 Household ICT Usage and Access Survey (results announcement)
smartphone_households_amman.notes: Household-level: a household having a smartphone does not mean every elderly member can use one. That is exactly the 'offline with a helper' case in the engine.

egov_use_individuals_jordan.source_name: MoDEE 2024 Household ICT Usage and Access Survey (results announcement)
egov_use_individuals_jordan.quote: 38.1% of individuals had accessed at least one e-government service
egov_use_individuals_jordan.notes: Context for the pitch: connectivity is near-universal, e-service use is not.

id_renewal_fee_jd.source_name: Confirmed by the team; add the CSPD link here if one is found
id_renewal_fee_jd.notes: JD 2 is the ID renewal fee, used as fee_jd in every scenario. The JD 1 the desk research cited (cspd.gov.jo e-services page) is for a different service: issuing a previously registered document electronically.

share_female.source_name: DoS figures as reported by The Jordan Times (Facebook post)
share_female.notes: Includes non-Jordanians (male-skewed migrant workforce). seed_census.py uses 53% male / 47% female, i.e. this figure as quoted by the research (tagged CITED there), for both its datasets.

disability_65_plus.source_name: UNFPA Arab States, Jordan country profile
disability_65_plus.notes: Any functional difficulty, all domains (seeing, hearing, walking...). Our seed models only mobility (limited/wheelchair), so this is an upper bound, not a direct input. PDF too large to verify automatically.

disability_overall_5_plus.source_name: 2015 Census (Washington Group) as cited by Humanity & Inclusion briefing paper 2023
disability_overall_5_plus.notes: All domains. Walking difficulty alone was reported at ~7% (secondary source).

female_labour_force_participation.notes: World Bank API was down (502) when we tried to confirm. Seed 'works' rates are employment, not participation.

bus_fare_jd_range.source_name: Transportation Research Interdisciplinary Perspectives article; BRT fare from expat guides
bus_fare_jd_range.notes: Context for BUS_FARE_JD only. Publisher blocked automated access (403). Our frozen BUS_FARE_JD 0.45 is an ASSUMPTION set before any scenario ran; it happens to lie inside this range.

bus_wait_peak_minutes.source_name: The Open Transportation Journal, vol 13, p 227
bus_wait_peak_minutes.notes: Context for BUS_FIRST_WAIT_MIN and BUS_WAIT_PLUS_TRANSFER_MIN only. A peak-hour wait; our frozen values (10 min first wait + 15 min per transfer) are ASSUMPTIONS, set for off-peak visits. BUS_WAIT_PLUS_TRANSFER_MIN is in the ±20% robustness check. A known gap, stated honestly.

district_population_2015.source_name: 2015 Census via GAM, as tabulated on Wikipedia 'Amman'
district_population_2015.notes: Seven of the 22 districts shown here; seed_census.py holds all 22 rows as quoted by the research and draws every citizen's district from their relative shares (VALIDATION.md, district table). Each district then maps to one of our 8 engine areas. Not yet checked against a GAM/DoS table, hence CITED_UNVERIFIED.

cspd_offices_amman.notes: The baseline scenario IS this network: the 7 offices are in sites.json (real: true) with their addresses from this page, located once with OpenStreetMap Nominatim (precision recorded per site). The 8 other sites are generic snap sites, one per engine area.

cspd_office_hours.source_name: CSPD's published office hours (cspd.gov.jo), read by the team on 2026-10-09
cspd_office_hours.notes: Used as the baseline hours of all 7 offices. The exact page URL was not recorded, so this stays TEAM_CONFIRMED; add the URL here (and 'retrieved') to make it ANCHORED. A Fri/Sat 10:00-14:00 line on CSPD's site is not modelled: it may be contact-centre hours.
